policy.admission: normal OS pressure and no new swap-outs for 60 seconds, load1 <=5, no competing Go tools
policy.runtime: stop owned workload on warning/critical pressure, new swap-outs or unreliable monitoring

workload.trigger: new system swap-outs observed; stopped owned workload

conclusions: The safety monitor stopped on actual new swapping, not a percentage threshold, test assertion failure or package timeout.
OS pressure remained normal even when swap-outs began; the separate swap-out condition mattered.
The first broad command was interrupted, so no full-partition command or full-suite pass is credited; some early package results are present in the partial log.
The approximately 6.69 GiB owned RSS peak is the measured process-tree sum at this stop, not the full suite's maximum or a universal minimum RAM requirement.
Swap counters are system-wide; telemetry does not identify which processes' pages were swapped.
This result does not prove that every 16 GiB Mac must fail; background applications, architecture, OS and cache state affect the envelope.
The independent 32 GiB experiment remains running; no final two-host comparison or permanent policy decision is made yet.
